properties.name: ROOT CAUSE (walked, measured), limitation 2: one auto-approve regex cannot tell a door read from a write because the command text carries only a tool name, and the read set (78 of 195 tools on main) is served nowhere on the CLI. Two things the requirement must also cover: export_graph and export_surface are annotated read-only yet write a file anywhere, overwrite included, and `--read-only` is silently ignored by `--call`
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL (root-cause, fetched fresh), triage agent D, on limitation 2 of art:vscode-call-door-field-report-2026-10-02 ("Approval on every call. One chat.tools.terminal.autoApprove regex cannot tell a read from a write"). Also covers idea 4 (the read/write verb split), which is already settled (dec:idea-a-shell-driven-agent-approves-reads-once-and-confirms-each-write) with this requirement as step 3; nothing new is minted for it.

① OBSERVED (reported): every --call prompts in VS Code. EXPECTED: reads auto-approved, writes prompted. NOT AFFECTED: the door itself classifies every tool. call_one_tool reads the served read_only_hint before it opens the store (crates/reflow2-mcp/src/main.rs:757-762 on origin/main 66620f7) and uses it only to decide snapshot-or-refuse on a held graph.

② PRECEDENT: the remedy is already recorded (this requirement, and the settled decision). Nothing recorded the mechanism below.

③ CANDIDATES: (a) the classification exists but is not in the command text, so a regex can only enumerate tool names; (b) the names exist but nothing served hands them over; (c) some flag already makes a prefix rule safe; (d) the annotation itself does not mean what auto-approval needs; (e) VS Code's matcher cannot express it (wrong observation).

⑤ MEASURED (0.77.0 release binary, scratch stores, log triage-D/measure.log):
- (a)+(b) HOLD. The command names a tool and nothing else about it. The 195 toolsnaps on main give 78 readOnlyHint=true and 117 not. No CLI call serves that split: find_tools items carry only tool, summary, parameters and score. So a regex today is a hand copy of 78 names that must be re-copied every release, which is the "hand-maintained list nobody checks" class.
- (c) REFUTED, and a hazard: `reflow2-mcp --read-only --call add_requirement ...` wrote the node, exit 0 (read back with get_node). call_one_tool never applies cli.read_only. Separate finding: fact:call-ignores-read-only-and-the-write-lands-2026-10-02.
- (d) HOLDS. readOnlyHint here means "does not write the GRAPH", not "no side effects". export_graph and export_surface are annotated read-only, take `path` and `overwrite`. Measured: export_graph with overwrite:true replaced an existing file, exit 0. compare_designs, merge_designs, describe_designs, certify_preservation, fork_point and analyze_alternatives read caller-named paths. A `reflow2 read` that is auto-approved would therefore auto-approve a file overwrite at any path. The requirement's MUST "every tool annotated read-only really writes nothing" has to count files too, or keep export_* out of the read verb.
- (e) PARTLY. VS Code's public docs (code.visualstudio.com/docs/agents/run/approvals) say rules are prefixes or /regex/ and match each subcommand unless matchCommandLine is true. So a `^reflow2 read ` prefix rule is expressible. How VS Code splits a heredoc body is not documented: NOT ESTABLISHED.

⑥ CLASS: the door's one piece of safety knowledge (read vs write) lives inside the process, and the approval decision is made outside it on text. The settled fix (a verb that refuses writers before opening anything) is the right shape because it moves the classification into the command text. Two conditions: the verb must enforce, not just document, and "read" must exclude file writes.

⑨ NOT ESTABLISHED: VS Code's handling of heredocs under autoApprove; whether the reporter's org policy allows autoApprove at all.
